newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel parliament clears Discount offer.
newsitem.headline: Israel parliament clears Discount offer.

text.p: Israel's parliamentary finance committee on Thursday gave the go-ahead for a secondary offering later this month of a 17 percent stake in Israel Discount Bank now held by the government.

The offering will be for shares and two series of warrants carrying exercise dates three and nine months after the offering. The prospectus is due to be published next week, according to the committee.

The government hopes to raise a minimum of 600 million shekels from the offering, 28 percent from the share tranches and the remainder from the warrants. Based on Discount's current market value, the offering is worth 675 million shekels.
Discount employees will be entitled to an offering equal to 1.7 percent of the bank.
IBI Underwriting and Investments, Eyal Securities and Issues, Leader Securities Issues and Clal Issuing are managing the offering.

The government floated 14.5 percent of Discount, Israel's third-largest commercial bank, in March 1996. The bank's shares had been removed from trading on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange after the government took the bank over in the wake of the 1983 bank shares crash.
If all the warrants are exercised, the latest offering will reduce the government's stake in the bank to 54 percent.
Market sources had said the government had planned to make an offering of warrants only, which they said would have discouraged foreign participation in the offering.
